note: Human/AI review ledger for content/tools/claim_source_audit.py. 'reviews': one verdict per claim, bound to the SHA-256 prefix of the claim text (an edit makes the entry stale and fails --check). 'locators': passages located in the source itself (sec:/art:/pp:), bound to the claim text hash. 'reference_levels': optional per-reference verification-level overrides. Written with --record-review / --record-locator. Never record a locator that was not actually read in the source.

reviews.basis: Source SRC-PMC11580817 is retracted (PubMed 'Retracted Publication', PMID 39575351; notice PMID 39791019). Kept on purpose as the documented retraction fixture: the app shows the retracted banner (claim.retracted.*) and the RAG pipeline excludes it (phase7_test, rag_pipeline_test). Owner decision: replace the claim's source (e.g. SRC-PMC12346081 INTRO: 'algor mortis (cooling of the body)') or keep as fixture.
Jurisdiction: 'separate criteria for biological specimens' now names the US ANSI/ASB 113 (example).
Jurisdiction and scope: ASB 113 labelled US, voluntary, excluding alcohols, CO, cyanide, metals.
Jurisdiction: ASB 113 labelled as a voluntary US standard.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), jones2010: elimination rate range 10-35 mg/100 mL/h, evidence-based survey; the document list (assumptions and their source) is practice advice resting on it.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), ketola2019: distributions of 183 drugs across all causes of death (median = normal PM level, upper percentiles = possible overdose); druid1997: femoral-blood compilation with fatal single-substance, multi-substance and control (other cause of death) groups. The earlier wording 'the same concentrations occur across different causes of death' is not stated in the abstracts; now: reported as distributions incl. a control group.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), pelissier2003: analyse specimens from different sampling sites to detect PMR; basic lipophilic drugs with large Vd susceptible but not only these; yarema2005: ideal site is a ligated or clamped femoral vein. The comparison of sites was wrongly attributed to yarema2005; now split between the two sources.
ASB 036 scope (fit for intended use) read on the official page; the pitfall ('habit is not justification') is practice advice, scope-level support only.

The word 'threshold' belongs to the sentence attributed to the Uzbek CPC (art:187:1); the JCGM/Gullberg part states only that the uncertainty budget (measurand, components, combination) is documented, which Gullberg's abstract states. JCGM 100 is cited for scope only.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), kugelberg2007: microbial/postmortem ethanol production is a recurring issue; vitreous humour and urine recommended; 'one blood sample proves neither' is the card's conservative inference.

Heuristic false positive. petersen2014 (phenolphthalein false positives from leghemoglobin) and barni2007 (luminol review) both describe the catalytic haemoglobin mechanism the sentence states. The 'dna' scope word comes from barni2007's used_for line ('effect on later serology/DNA'), and the sentence makes no immunoassay claim. Checked by Claude against both used_for records and the card text, 2026-10-10.
Same johnston2008 heuristic trigger; the sentence lists the alternatives to benzidine and does not generalise any animal-restricted finding. Checked by Claude, 2026-10-10.

Same johnston2008 'primate-specific' wording triggering the animal-scope heuristic; the cited point (a DNA profile obtained straight from kit buffer) is not animal-restricted. Checked by Claude, 2026-10-10.

Heuristic false positive: the 'animal' flag comes from johnston2008's used_for phrase 'OBTI is primate-specific'. The study compares kits on human dried bloodstains, and the card states the primate specificity of OBTI in the very next sentence. Checked by Claude, 2026-10-10.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), drummer2004: 'no concentration of a drug of abuse can be interpreted in isolation'; ferner2008 / kennedy2010: tables of lethal concentrations misleading (registry used_for; abstracts re-read). Claim matches; drummer2004 concerns drugs of abuse (the card applies the principle to CO as a general PM-toxicology rule - expert to confirm).
delvau2024 is a swine model: the oxygen-administration factor is now marked '(shown in an animal model)'; the other factors are unchanged.
delvau2024 is a swine model: marked '(shown in an animal model)'.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10: delvau2024 = 'On a swine model' (experimental swine, 940 ppm CO until COHb 30%); bi-compartmental half-life and slight rebound. The claim was stated without the species; now says swine experiment, not transferable directly to humans (species scope).

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), kugelberg2007: 'If ethanol remains unabsorbed in the stomach at the time of death ... continued local diffusion into surrounding tissues and central blood'. Claim matches; automatic scope flag was a false positive (stomach is the diffusion source, not the specimen).

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), barnhill2007: serum/whole-blood ratio is concentration-dependent (about 1.12-1.18), 'precluding a generally applicable SAC/BAC conversion factor' (212 patients). Claim states exactly this; not a general rule beyond the abstract.
Jurisdiction and scope: 'in toxicology identification criteria are set by a separate standard' - now the US ANSI/ASB 113, excluding alcohols, CO, cyanide and metals.
PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10: drummer2004: benzodiazepines are 'particularly prone to degradation'. 'Especially nitro compounds' is not in the abstract and was removed.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10: uchiyama2008 analysed designated substances by TLC under two different solvent conditions; it does not state that one system is not enough. The 'at least two systems' rule is now marked as a practical recommendation derived from the textbook's three systems.

Textbook p.46 located; kato2001 abstract: citric acid/acetic anhydride reagent is class-selective for tertiary amines. Automatic method flag (TLC vs colour test) is a false positive: the claim concerns the reagent, not the TLC step.

Jurisdiction and scope: ASB 113 is a US voluntary standard; the registry scope (official page) excludes alcohols/routine volatiles, carbon monoxide, cyanide and metals - now stated; the card is a general method comparison.

saitman2014 abstract: immunoassay positives presumptive until confirmed by a second independent technique (urine drug screens). SWGDRUG IIIB.3.1/3.2 (PDF re-read): a Category B or C technique alone is insufficient. Earlier text said a screening result is 'never' reported as definitive and is always confirmed by a technique of a different principle: narrowed to what the two sources state.
Jurisdiction: separate standards named as the US ANSI/ASB 113 and 098.
Jurisdiction: 'the forensic toxicology method-validation standard requires' named as the US ANSI/ASB 036.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), de Zeeuw 1992 and 1994 abstracts: Rf correction with a reference mixture on each plate gives corrected values compatible with databases; 1997 abstract: databases and validation needed. Wording 'proposed' is within these abstracts.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), dezeeuw1994: the abstract supports only the Rf-correction mixture on every plate (accuracy and reproducibility improved). The earlier text also required standards and negative/positive controls and said results are not interpreted without them; that part is now marked 'general laboratory-practice requirement' and no longer attributed to the paper.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), de Zeeuw 1992/1994: high temperature and humidity shift Rf values (up to 20-30 Rf units) and worsen reproducibility; correction with a reference mixture on each plate improves it. Claim matches.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), siek1997: detection limits 5-200 ng per spot, depending on the drug; kato2001: detectability depends on the reagent. 'Negative result does not prove absence' is the standard logical consequence.

Textbook pp.153-155 located (earlier TOKS audit). maurer2004 abstract: GC-MS (EI full scan) is the method of choice for screening, LC-MS supplements for polar, thermolabile, low-dose drugs; it does not say 'no conclusion without instrumental confirmation'. Now: maurer attributed to the screening statement, confirmation rule marked as a general principle.
Jurisdiction: 'a dedicated standard' named as the US ANSI/ASB 036.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10: pollanen1998 = six homicidal-drowning case reports, diatoms recovered from femoral bone marrow incl. one grossly decomposed and one burned body; bortolotti2004: passive penetration cannot be excluded in highly transformed cadavers. The earlier mechanistic statement ('siliceous frustule resists decomposition, so the test is applicable') is in neither abstract; replaced by the case evidence plus the caveat.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10: hurlimann2000 (contamination-free sampling/preparation; water samples from surface and bed) and tyr2025 (contamination and standardisation need further research). 'Blank controls in every batch must be run' is not in either abstract; now marked as a general laboratory-practice requirement and not attributed to the papers.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), piette2006: 'the ideal diagnostic test as definite proof for drowning still needs to be established' (review, published 2005-12-27 online, Forensic Sci Int 163:1-9, 2006). Claim within the abstract.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), pounder1990: highest levels in central vessels, lowest in peripheral; unknown site undermines the reference value of databases. Wording now states exactly this instead of a reporting rule.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), drummer2004: heroin, morphine glucuronides, cocaine, benzodiazepines prone to degradation; mcallister2008: cyanide inherently unstable in cadavers and stored samples. 'A negative/low result does not prove absence' is a logical consequence of documented instability; not stated verbatim in the abstracts.
Jurisdiction: 'recommendations are followed' (sounds binding) changed to 'taken into account (for example the US ANSI/ASB 037)'.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10: kintz2017 says hair gives a retrospective exposure history (weeks to years depending on hair length); it does not say 'only indirect information about prior use' nor that tolerance cannot be measured in a PM specimen. The latter is now marked as a general toxicological principle.

Jurisdiction: ANSI/ASB BPR 037 is a US (AAFS Standards Board) voluntary recommendation; the card said 'the toxicology consensus body' without naming it. Now names ASB, states voluntary / not binding in Uzbekistan.
Jurisdiction: ASB 156 named as US ASB voluntary recommendation (scope read on the official page only).

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10: flanagan2005: blood 5 mL from two distinct peripheral sites (preferably femoral veins), not central vessels; guidelines cover labelling. 'Never pooled in one container' is not in the abstract and was removed.

PubMed abstract re-read 2026-10-10 (NCBI E-utilities / PubMed MCP), skopp2004 / dinis2010: advantages and limitations of preservation procedures discussed; flanagan2005: preservative added to a portion of the blood. Claim matches.

ASB BPR 156 was read only on the official page (scope). 'Existing recommendations are adapted to laboratory and jurisdictional requirements' went beyond the scope statement; now: the US ASB 156 gives guidance on collection, amounts, preservatives, storage; adaptation is the laboratory's responsibility (general practice).
